title: A tour through the southern and western territories of the United States (John Pope)
evidence: 'Futchu, a Duck. Pinnua, a Turkey... Iste na af•cha? where are you going?' – compiled with the Little King of Broken Arrow
novelty_basis: Not cited in Glottolog Creek refs I could see; Pilling Muskhogean bibliography likely lists Pope (not verified). Web search: only bibliographic/historical mentions, no linguistic edition.
notes: Includes Latin-veiled sexual vocabulary, dialogue phrases and Creek hydronyms near Pensacola; an early (1791) Creek list predating Hawkins.

title: A series of Indostan letters (Bartholomew Burges), New York
evidence: 'Budgeroes, barges or gallies. Choquees, watchmen... Chunam, cement. Cheerabund, virgins.'
novelty_basis: First American book on India (scroll.in); glossary noted only in catalogue records; not used in Hobson-Jobson/Anglo-Indian lexicography as far as found.
notes: Anglo-Indian trade glossary for American merchants; value is for history of Anglo-Indian lexicon, not language documentation.

title: The habitable world described (John Trusler), vol. 3
evidence: 'ENGLISH | EASTJAIK. | WOGUL. | MORDVINE. Two. | Kat. | Kijtti. | Kaftta.'
novelty_basis: Derivative of Georgi's Russian ethnography (well known source); compilation itself obscure.

title: The habitable world described (Trusler), vol. 6
novelty_basis: From Cook/King 3rd voyage comparative table (well known).

title: The habitable world described (Trusler), vol. 1
evidence: 'A River, Jocki... Water, Kietze. A Bear, Muriet.'

title: A voyage to the Pacific Ocean (Cook 3rd voyage), American edition
evidence: 'Quadne, a woman. Eve'rai, the eye. Muidje, the nose.'
novelty_basis: Anderson's Tasmanian list, widely used (Plomley, Crowley & Dixon).
notes: Known but extinct language; US reprint.

title: Three years travels through the interior parts of North-America (Carver), Philadelphia
evidence: 'Water, Nebbi... Woman, Ickwee... Thank you, Megwatch'

title: A new voyage round the world (Hawkesworth/Cook), New York
language_as_named: New Holland; Otaheite; numerals of islands
notes: Also ECCO K062748.002/.003, K021793.003/.004 (Parkinson-derived, incl. Māori, Savu), K085977.000.

title: Madagascar: or, Robert Drury's journal
evidence: 'VII. A VOCABULARY of the Madagascar Language'
novelty_basis: Drury vocabulary well known (Grandidier, Parker Pearson).

title: An historical and geographical description of Formosa (Psalmanazar)
notes: Also K108002.000 (1710). Not a real language.
